pr_title: Fix(plan): sweeps skip the plan's own source document
verdict: NOT READY TO MERGE - minor findings pending Phase 5: M1, M2, M3, M4, M5
strengths: Each new test can fail for the stated reason: without the skip, the spec shows as an unclassified hit in the tree, and as a classified file without a hit at the base.

The base-revision test builds a real commit after the base and asserts both the working tree and the base rev, so it covers the case the sweep_problems docstring names, a spec added on the plan's branch.
The tests use real git repos via make_project and call sweep_problems directly, so nothing is stubbed and nothing asserts on mock calls.

The absolute-path case uses str(root / SPEC), which exercises backslash handling on Windows, and the outside-the-repo case sits under tmp_path/elsewhere, outside the project folder, so it really tests the ValueError branch of source_path.
The skip is applied symmetrically to the classified set and the hit set, so a spec committed on the plan's branch cannot raise 'classified but has no hit' when the sweep runs at the base rev.
sweep_problems computes the skipped set once per call, outside the sweep loop, and the sweep_hits signature is unchanged, so the other sweep_hits callers are unaffected.

source_path resolves both sides before relative_to, so an absolute source_document under a symlinked or differently-cased root still maps to the repo-relative path, and the ValueError case degrades to None rather than raising.
The new docstring text states why the source document is skipped, and the write-plan SKILL.md already lists it beside the plans folder as never a hit.

write-plan SKILL.md sweeps row (line 63) matches plan_checks.sweep_problems: the plans folder and the plan's source_document are dropped from both the hit set and the classified set, so 'never hits' is accurate on both sides of the comparison.

The v0.7.0 release table moves harness to 0.65.1 in step with the plugin.json patch bump, and the header's minor-release rationale stays correct since harness already bumped its minor within this release.

write-plan SKILL.md:63 states the new exclusion in the existing sweeps table row, and the wording ('never hits') matches the code, which drops the source document from both the grep hits and the classified set so neither the unclassified nor the stale-classification check fires on it.

The skill package stays coherent: no rename, the Related links (scripts/plan.py, lib/harness_lib/plan_models.py, schemas/ActionPlan.schema.json) all exist, and the `--spec` path `new` stores (plan.py:180, repo-relative POSIX) is the shape source_path in plan_checks.py:272-282 expects.
The plugin version bump and the docs/RELEASES/v0.7.0.md row and change line were updated together with the skill text.

The skip runs on both sides (`classified - skipped` and `hits -= skipped`), so plans that already classified their spec as a workaround keep passing instead of turning into 'classified but has no hit'.
test_a_spec_committed_after_the_base_passes_the_sweep_at_the_base reproduces the real failure against real git: a spec committed after the base, checked both in the tree and at the base rev.
The tests are behavioral throughout: real repos from make_project and real git grep, with no stubs. The outside-the-repo case pins the fallback with an exact problem line.
The SKILL.md table, the patch bump to 0.65.1 and the v0.7.0 release table all moved together with the code.

minor.name: Release note entry lacks its PR number
minor.summary:
docs/RELEASES/v0.7.0.md:18 adds the entry 'Fix(plan): sweeps skip the plan's own source document ...' without a PR reference, while every other line in the Changes list leads with its PR number ('#248 Feature(todo): ...', '#244 Feature(harness): ...'). This change ships as PR #249, so the entry breaks the list's format and the release body loses the link to the PR.

Also (roast): Every other Changes line in docs/RELEASES/v0.7.0.md starts with its PR number (`#248 ...`, `#244 ...`). The new line at :18 starts with a bare `Fix(plan): ...`, although this change is PR #249.
fix: Prefix the entry with the PR number: '- #249 Fix(plan): sweeps skip the plan's own source document, so a spec committed on the plan's branch no longer blocks the freeze'
Prefix the line: `- #249 Fix(plan): sweeps skip the plan's own source document, so a spec committed on the plan's branch no longer blocks the freeze`.

minor.name: source_path docstring promises an outside-root check it applies only to absolute paths
minor.summary:
The docstring says source_path returns None when the document is 'unset or outside root'. A relative source_document is returned verbatim as_posix with no containment check, so '../elsewhere/spec.md' (or a backslash path on a POSIX host) comes back as a non-None string. The result is harmless, since it never matches a git grep path, but the contract text and the code disagree.

Also (roast): source_path returns None for an absolute source_document outside root (plan_checks.py:279-282), and `plan.py new` stores an absolute --spec verbatim (scripts/plan.py:180, via skeleton at :173). A plan created with an absolute spec path in the main checkout and checked or frozen from a worktree (or the reverse) therefore gets no skip, and the spec blocks the freeze exactly as before the fix. Nothing reports it either. The fix works for anyone who passes a relative path, which is most people, so this is a sharp edge rather than a hole.
fix: Narrow the docstring: 'None when unset, or when an absolute path lies outside root; a relative path is returned as written.'
Or normalize the relative branch through os.path.normpath and return None when the result starts with '..'.

Store source_document repo-relative at creation: in cmd_new, turn an absolute args.spec inside repo into `path.resolve().relative_to(repo.resolve()).as_posix()` (or refuse an absolute spec outside the repo), so source_path never has to guess which checkout it came from.
Have `plan.py check` report a problem line when source_document is absolute and outside the checked root, so the silent no-skip shows up.

minor.name: Docstring says the plans folder is skipped on both sides; it is not
minor.summary: sweep_problems' docstring (plan_checks.py:288-289) says the source document is skipped on both sides "like the plans folder". The plans folder is skipped only on the hit side, in sweep_hits (:259). A classified plans-folder path still fails as "classified but has no hit" (:302). The comparison promises symmetry the code does not have. SKILL.md:63 states it correctly ("are never hits").
fix: Reword to: "The plan's own source document is skipped on both sides; the plans folder is already dropped from the hits by sweep_hits. The document names the symbols the sweeps search for, and a spec committed on the plan's branch is absent at the base."

minor.name: sweeps field description in plan_models still says every hit file fails unclassified
minor.summary: write-plan SKILL.md:63 now states that the plans folder and the plan's own source_document are never sweep hits, matching sweep_problems in plan_checks.py:285-303 (the source path is subtracted from both the grep hits and the classified set). The ActionPlan.sweeps Field description in plan_models.py:431-434, which the SKILL.md Related list points to as 'the one definition of a plan' and which is generated into schemas/ActionPlan.schema.json, still says check 'fails on a file with hits that `hits` does not classify, or a classified file with none', with no mention of either exclusion. A plan author reading the schema gets a rule the driver no longer applies to the spec file (and never applied to the plans folder).
fix: Extend the sweeps description in plan_models.py:431-434 with 'The plans folder and the plan's own `source_document` are skipped on both sides.' and regenerate plugins/harness/schemas/ActionPlan.schema.json from the models.

minor.name: New sweep helpers duplicate sweep_plan and split the sweep tests
minor.summary: source_plan repeats the sweeps literal that sweep_plan builds (same id and pattern), and the SPEC and CODE_HITS constants plus the helper sit mid-section, between test_untracked_files_count_and_the_plans_folder_does_not and test_a_tracked_file_under_an_ignored_folder_still_counts. The file otherwise puts each section's helper at the top of the section. The result is two helpers that build the same sweep and a sweeps section split in two.
fix: Move SPEC, CODE_HITS and source_plan up beside sweep_plan (line 175), and let sweep_plan take an optional source argument (sweep_plan(hits, source=None)) so one helper serves both.
Move the four new tests after test_a_bad_pattern_is_a_problem so the existing sweep tests stay contiguous.
